title: Adding the first honey super in spring
subtitle: Timing and placing the first super to catch the early season flow.
excerpt: The first super goes on when bees are filling the top brood box and the spring flow is imminent. Too early and the bees ignore it; too late and a sudden flow causes the colony to swarm from sheer congestion. The timing call is made by reading the colony, not by the calendar.
sourceNotes: NBU Beekeeper's Toolkit (2024), section on swarm prevention and space management. BBKA Advisory Leaflet on spring management. Frank Pearson, Bee-keeping for All (1923), Internet Archive, chapter on honey production. AHDB Agriculture, OSR flowering windows for the UK (2023).

glossaryTerms.definition: A shallow or medium hive box placed above the brood chamber where bees store surplus honey for harvesting. Frames in a super are usually shorter than brood frames.
A period of abundant nectar production in the landscape, during which forager bees bring in more nectar than the colony immediately needs.
A flat grid of wire or plastic placed between the brood chamber and the super, with gaps large enough for workers but too small for the queen, keeping brood out of the honey boxes.

content.text: Adding the first
super
in spring is one of the most important spring management decisions. Too early and the bees spend energy heating an empty box rather than building up. Too late and a sudden oil seed rape
flow
or fruit blossom flush finds the colony with nowhere to put nectar, triggering swarm preparation from congestion alone.
When to super up
Open the hive on a warm still day, preferably mid-morning to early afternoon when the forager population is out. The colony needs a super when all the signs below are present together:
The top brood box (or single brood box) is covered in bees on every frame when you lift the crown board.
Bees are storing nectar and capping honey in the top two or three frames of the brood box.
The nearby spring forage is about to open or is already flowering: OSR, fruit blossom, hawthorn.

UK timing reference: OSR flow typically runs from mid-April to mid-May depending on the region and variety. Fruit blossom follows from late April into May. In a mild season, a strong colony that overwintered well may need its first super by late March.
What you need
A drawn super. Frames with drawn-out foundation work best; foundation-only frames are accepted more slowly by a building colony.
A
queen excluder
if you want honey free of brood. Fit it below the super.
Your smoker and hive tool.
Fitting the super
Light the smoker and suit up before approaching the hive. A couple of puffs under the crown board settle the colony before you lift the brood box lid.

Confirm the colony is ready: lift the crown board and check that bees cover most frames. If bees occupy only four or five frames, the colony is not yet strong enough and the super can wait another two weeks.
Fit the queen excluder directly on top of the brood box. A wire excluder lies flat; push any up-standing wires flat with your hive tool so the brood box can sit flush beneath it.
Place the super on top of the excluder. Set the crown board on top of the super, replace the roof.
Note the date in your apiary log. Check back in 10 to 14 days: if bees are working the super frames, the
flow
is on.
Adding a second super

Add a second super when bees cover seven or eight frames in the first one and are beginning to cap honey. Place the second super below the first (between the excluder and the first super). Bees fill the lower box first, which keeps them moving upward and away from the excluder. A colony working a strong OSR flow can fill a super in two weeks and needs a second one promptly.

attrs.cue: Bees are not entering the super after ten days
attrs.cause: Flow has not started, colony is not yet strong enough, or bees are reluctant to cross the excluder
attrs.fix: Move one frame of bees, with adhering workers but no brood, from the top of the brood box up into the super. This primes bees to work the new box. If no flow is happening outside, wait: bees will not store surplus when there is no incoming nectar.

attrs.cue: OSR honey is setting solid in the comb
attrs.cause: Oil seed rape honey granulates quickly in the comb
attrs.fix: Extract OSR honey within three to four weeks of capping. Once it sets in comb it is very difficult to extract. Check the super earlier than you would for summer honey.

attrs.cue: Swarm cells in the brood box despite adding a super
attrs.cause: Supering does not prevent swarming, it only removes one congestion trigger
attrs.fix: Continue standard swarm inspections every seven days. Adding a super is not a substitute for managing the colony's swarm impulse through inspection and queen cell control.
